newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU ministers agree road traffic pollution deal.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers agree road traffic pollution deal.

text.p: European Union environment ministers boosted chances of an earlier-than-planned cut in traffic fumes on Friday when they tightened parts of a draft package of engine emission and fuel quality standards for cars.
"After long and difficult discussions, the Council reached a unanimous political agreement on the first part of the so-called Auto-oil programme," the ministers said in a statement.
"It means that we will get to our air quality objectives quicker," one European Commission official said.

On the table were two Commission proposals drawn up after years of research work with the European oil and car industries and launched last year amid widespread criticism of the standards set and methods used.

Ministers cut from 200 parts per million to 150 parts per million proposed mandatory limits on the sulphur to be allowed in petrol from the year 2000, a move which will curb the damaging effects of sulphur dioxide on catalytic converters fitted to car exhausts.

But they included an opt-out, which Greece and Portugal said they would definitely take up, allowing countries to stay the application of new standards for up to three years in the case of "severe socio-economic problems".
Ministers also halved allowed benzene levels in petrol to one percent from the year 2000, meaning reduced airborne pollution by the cancer-causing chemical.

Friday's deal, which must win the approval of the European Parliament before adoption, also introduced checks on aromatics in fuel, lead, and set indicative fuel norms for 2005 where in the original proposal there were none.
